cross_response_observations: Seven of the eight responses contain arithmetic_recursion_error, showing that even when models attempt DP computation, they frequently make mistakes in the execution. Three responses (A, B, G) claim false periodic patterns, with A and B asserting period-4 and G asserting period-9 based on a wrong move set. Two responses (A, B) use arbitrary pattern heuristics without DP verification, claiming P-positions follow simple periodic formulas. Four responses are truncated (D, E, F, G), with E providing only 18 characters and D only 85. Move set errors are common: B excludes 1 (interpreting duplicate Fibonacci values as exclusion), F includes 0 (using F_0=0), and G uses a completely wrong enumeration (Lucas-style 1,2,4,7,11...). Response C globally swaps P/N labels (confused_pn_convention) while D only inverts the base case (base_case_set_to_n). Response E misapplies Sprague-Grundy theory. Response H non-terminates, looping through the same position definitions repeatedly. No response produces the correct 101-character classification. The most common defect type is arithmetic errors in DP execution, followed by move set misinterpretations and false periodicity claims.
